decisions.reason: The shipped row cited the replication team's own Stage 1 Registered Report protocol (Shan et al., 2015, 10.7717/peerj.1232) rather than the original study whose findings were re-tested (Thadani-Mulero et al., 2014, 10.1158/0008-5472.can-13-2876). Per the codebook, a registered-report protocol is ruled out in favor of the paper reporting the tested original finding.

decisions.quote: Additionally, we were unable to see any effect from the docetaxel treatment from either cell line, which may have been due to this difference in growth rate between the two tumor lines, or potentially to a compromised quality of the docetaxel reagent. While a future study could include a positive quality control for the reagent, it is outside the scope of this replication study as it was not factored into the plan at the stage of the Registered Report. It was unexpected that there would be such a lack of response to the docetaxel treatment and thus a positive quality control test was not included in the Registered Report and thus not replicated here. These factors contribute to a strongly inconclusive replication attempt of the original paper as we are unable to demonstrate that the ARv7 expression resulted in the difference in docetaxel treatment.
decisions.reason: Evaluated against the resolved tested original (Thadani-Mulero et al., 2014). Although the shipped coding relied on an individual comparison for LuCaP 86.2 tumor growth, the authors explicitly state an overall verdict in the Discussion that the attempt is 'not a strong test of the original hypothesis' and is a 'strongly inconclusive replication attempt of the original paper' due to undetectable ARv7 in LuCaP 23.1, slow tumor growth, N20 antibody failure, and lack of a positive quality control for the docetaxel reagent. Under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1, this special overall verdict governs and maps to 'uninformative'.

The study collected new experimental data (mouse xenograft tumor growth assays and Western blots) to re-test previously published findings from Thadani-Mulero et al. (2014), which is a replication under the codebook.

decisions.location: Abstract (lines 94-110); Introduction (lines 144-166); Results and Discussion (lines 330-450); References (line 532).
decisions.quote: Thadani-Mulero and colleagues reported that ARv567 and ARv7 responded differently to docetaxel in their 2014 Cancer Research paper. They found that the ARv567 variant was heavily associated with microtubules, while the ARv7 variant was not, which resulted in a significant decrease of nuclear accumulation of ARv567 but not ARv7 with docetaxel treatment. They performed a xenograft tumor growth assay on two different prostate cancer cell lines: LuCaP 86.2, which expresses wild-type androgen receptor (AR) and ARv567, and LuCaP 23.1, which expresses wild-type AR and ARv7. They reported that docetaxel treatment reduced tumor growth significantly in tumors derived from LuCaP 86.2 cells, while tumors derived from LuCaP 23.1 did not show tumor growth reduction, suggesting that docetaxel affects the AR splice variants differently.

initial_expert_decision.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. The paper 7c729ad77091cc25 (Shan et al., 2018, PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.4661) is a Replication Study from the Prostate Cancer Foundation-Movember Foundation Reproducibility Initiative. The single shipped row (input_row_index 1162, Shan et al., 2015, 'Registered report: androgen receptor splice variants determine taxane sensitivity in prostate cancer', PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.1232) is the replicating authors' own Stage 1 Registered Report protocol describing their planned methodology, not the original empirical study whose findings are tested. Per the codebook rule ('Before naming any entry, rule out: another work by the same authors; a registered-report protocol or preregistration versus the paper reporting the original finding'), the actual original study being empirically replicated is Thadani-Mulero et al. (2014) ('Androgen receptor splice variants determine taxane sensitivity in prostate cancer', Cancer Research 74:2270-2282, DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.can-13-2876), specifically Figures 6A and 6B (xenograft tumor growth response to docetaxel in LuCaP 86.2 and LuCaP 23.1 prostate cancer lines and Western blot analysis of AR splice variants). Because only the 2015 protocol was shipped, the true original empirical target Thadani-Mulero et al. (2014) is genuinely missing. (Luna's mechanical quote validation error was due to collapsing XML line breaks around inline citations in the text extract.)
